answer: Each identity registers one jetty relay post in a harbor whisper network, locking a 70 bond. The harbor master gives it one whisper notice; it signs and forwards it to the next jetty post in-window. An auditor checks signatures and chain uniqueness, burning a missing or copied relay bond. Fee is 34+6(k-1) for the kth identity; the 1,000th pays 6,028, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,031,000 plus 70,000 locked. An honest relay pays 34 once, bond back after a clean epoch. A rented-relay ring fails: its key is bound to its own entry, so one post cannot forward for many in a window.
